title: Pig's Sleepy Count
lesson: Counting slowly helps you feel calm and ready to sleep
summary: Pig cannot sleep, so Owl and Cat take him on a quiet night walk to count stars, flowers and ripples until he feels sleepy.

steps.say: Night had come. Little Pig was in his cosy bed, but his eyes were wide open.

steps.text: Oink. I cannot sleep. My tummy feels wiggly.

steps.say: Pig tried to count sheep. But there were no sheep in his room.

steps.text: One... oh dear. Where are my sheep?

steps.say: Tap, tap, tap. Someone was at the window.

steps.text: Hoo hoo. Pig, are you awake? Come and count with me.
Count what, Owl? It is dark outside.
Count the sleepy things of the night. Follow me, hoo hoo.

steps.say: Pig put on his slippers. Off they went, very slowly, into the quiet garden.
The garden was dark and calm. Above them, the sky was full of twinkles.

steps.text: Look up, Pig. The stars are coming out, one by one.

steps.say: One little star. Twinkle.
Two little stars. Twinkle, twinkle.

steps.text: Three! Three stars! Can you count them with me?

steps.say: Four stars, and five stars. Five sleepy stars, shining softly.

steps.text: Now say it slowly. One, two, three, four, five. Sleepy stars.
Ahh. My tummy feels a little less wiggly.

steps.say: Next, they walked past the garden fence. The flowers had closed their petals for the night.

steps.text: Flowers go to sleep too. Count them, Pig.
One pink flower. Two purple flowers. Three yellow flowers.

steps.say: Three sleepy flowers. Pink, purple and yellow. All with their heads bowed down.

steps.text: Goodnight, pink. Goodnight, purple. Goodnight, yellow.

steps.say: Someone soft stepped out of the shadows. It was Cat, stretching and yawning.

steps.text: Meow. Purr. Are you counting? I love counting. It makes me purr.
Yes! We are counting the sleepy things. Come with us.
Purr, purr. I will count in my softest voice.

steps.say: So three friends tiptoed on, quiet as a whisper, to the pond.
Past the garden, the forest was dark and still. But look! Tiny lights were blinking.

steps.text: Fireflies! Let us count their little lights.
Blink. One firefly. Blink. Two fireflies.
Blink, blink. Three. And four. Four glowing fireflies.

steps.say: Four fireflies, glowing gold. They blinked slowly, as if they were sleepy too.

steps.text: Can you blink slowly like a firefly? Blink, blink, blink.

steps.say: Pig blinked. Cat blinked. Owl blinked. Their eyes felt heavier and heavier.

steps.text: Mmm. Counting makes me sleepy too. Let us visit the pond.

steps.say: The pond was still and silver. A little duck floated near the reeds with her head tucked in.

steps.text: Shh. Duck is nearly asleep. Let us whisper.
Hello, Duck. We are counting sleepy things. Can we count you?
Quack, quack... yes. I am one sleepy duck.

steps.say: Plip! A ripple spread across the water. One ripple.
Plip! Two ripples, getting bigger and bigger.

steps.text: Two ripples. And one duck. That makes... three!
Mmm. Three is a cosy number. Goodnight, friends.

steps.say: The ripples melted away. The pond was quiet again. Everyone yawned a great big yawn.
On the way home, the sky was a soft, deep purple. The moon was round and gentle.

steps.text: Owl, how many things did we count tonight?
Five stars. Three flowers. One duck. Two ripples. That is lots of sleepy things.
And one moon. Do not forget the moon.
Ooh! And that is one, two, three... four friends.

steps.say: Pig looked at his friends, and his tummy felt warm and still.

steps.text: I think I can sleep now. Thank you for counting with me.
Purr. Sweet dreams, Pig.

steps.say: Cat and Owl waved goodbye. Pig walked home, step by sleepy step.
Back in his room, Pig climbed into bed. His blanket was soft and warm.

steps.text: One moon. Two ears. Three... yawn... four...

steps.say: Pig counted all the sleepy things again, slowly, slowly, slowly.

steps.text: Five stars, three flowers, four fireflies... goodnight.

steps.say: His eyes grew heavy. His tummy was calm. Pig was fast asleep.
Goodnight, Pig. Goodnight, stars. Goodnight, everyone. The end!
